key_insight: LACUNA introduces a testbed for checking whether LLM unlearning actually removes information from inside the model, not just from its outputs. It highlights that evaluating only output behavior can miss hidden residual knowledge after unlearning.
problem_solved: Existing unlearning benchmarks mainly measure whether a model stops producing sensitive information, but they do not verify if the information is truly erased from the model's internal parameters or representations. This paper addresses the gap in evaluating localization precision for unlearning methods.
method: Proposes LACUNA, a benchmark/testbed focused on localization precision in LLM unlearning.
Evaluates localize-first, unlearn-second methods by examining whether they target the correct parameters or regions of the model.
Moves beyond output-only evaluation to assess whether knowledge is removed from the model itself.
impact: This matters for AI practitioners because safer unlearning requires more than suppressing outputs—it needs genuine removal of sensitive knowledge. LACUNA can help researchers compare unlearning methods more rigorously and reduce privacy and compliance risks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing localize-first -> unlearn-second -> evaluation
Side-by-side comparison of output-level vs internal-knowledge evaluation
Model heatmap highlighting targeted parameters or layers
Icon set for PII, privacy, and memory erasure
paper_title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
paper_authors: Matteo Boglioni, Thibault Rousset, Siva Reddy, Marius Mosbach, Verna Dankers
